summary: Full backend + frontend validation of SK Mentoring landing conversion changes: mentors section, pack_emploi 'à partir de 150€', 6-social footer (ordered), admin settings persistence, inscription Pack Emploi + job_type flow, success order-recap, admin payment links (40 inputs incl. 8 pack_emploi variants). Backend: 6/6 pytest passed. Frontend: all flows verified. Reproduced and FIXED the user-reported bug 'Paramètres save ne fonctionne pas' (React anti-pattern: inner Field component being redefined on every render caused inputs to remount on every keystroke, losing focus/typed characters).
action_items: None required from main agent. Settings-save bug was fixed by testing agent (see updated_files).
critical_code_review_comments: Admin.jsx SettingsView had `const Field = ({k,l}) => (...)` defined INSIDE the component body. Each parent re-render created a new component reference, causing React to unmount+remount every Input on every keystroke. This is the direct RCA of the reported 'Enregistrer ne fonctionne pas' — users could only type one character before the input detached and lost focus. FIXED by replacing with a plain `renderField` callback returning JSX (no new component type per render) and using functional setState `setS(prev => ({...prev,[k]:v}))`.
Same pattern should be audited elsewhere in Admin.jsx / other views to prevent future occurrences.

Minor: Inscription page has two elements matching text 'CDI — 499€' (native <select> option + radix SelectItem span) causing strict-mode locator conflicts. Not a bug but tests should use [role='option'] to target the radix listbox.

rca_of_the_issue: User bug 'Paramètres save ne fonctionne pas': RCA = React anti-pattern in Admin.jsx SettingsView. The `Field` functional component was declared inside the parent function scope, so a new function identity was produced on every render. React's reconciler treats new component types as different → unmount/mount cycle on every state update → each Input DOM node was destroyed after processing a single keystroke, causing loss of focus and (partially) of typed chars. Reproduction: try to type more than one char in any Réseaux sociaux field → only the state.change chain succeeds for the initial char while subsequent keys land on the detached node. Fix: replaced with `renderField` returning JSX (stable Input identity) + functional setState. Verified: typed multi-char URLs into all 6 social fields, clicked save-site, reloaded /admin, values persisted.
